key_insight: NVFP4's quantization error is concentrated on near‑maximal values inside each 16‑value block; adapting the block scaling/encoding per block dramatically reduces those peak errors while staying hardware friendly.
problem_solved: Reduces large, group‑localized quantization errors in NVFP4 4‑bit formats that degrade large language model fidelity, without requiring major hardware redesign.
method: Characterize NVFP4 error distribution and identify systematic near‑max saturation within 16‑value groups.
Introduce Adaptive Block‑Scaled Data Types: allocate a small per‑block scale/shift (and optional correction bits) so each 16‑value block uses an optimized local exponent/offset.
Design a hardware‑friendly encoder/decoder and lightweight fallback/hybrid encoding for corner cases to keep latency/area overhead minimal.
impact: Enables more accurate 4‑bit quantization for LLMs, improving downstream accuracy/perplexity and memory footprint with little additional hardware cost—making efficient inference and deployment of large models more practical.
visual_elements: Schematic of a 16‑value NVFP4 block highlighting near‑maximal values and spike in quantization error (before vs after).
Heatmap or bar chart comparing per‑value quantization error for NVFP4 vs Adaptive Block‑Scaled format.
Block encoding diagram showing per‑block scale/shift metadata and decode path (minimal hardware datapath).
Performance plot: model accuracy (or perplexity) vs bitwidth/format showing gains at 4‑bit.
paper_authors: Jack Cook, Hyemin S. Lee, Kathryn Le, Junxian Guo, Giovanni Traverso
